transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Greene (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Tom Li (CTO - Marlin), Sarah Nguyen (Head of ML), Mark Rivera (Infra)
Shared links: pricing deck (https://redwood.example/pricing-deck), benchmark template (https://redwood.example/benchmarks/marlin), security docs (SAML/SOC2 link noted)

[00:00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, i'm alex from redwood - i'll kick off, quick agenda — cost economics, hosting options, and then we can do q and a and next steps
[00:00:12] Tom: thanks alex, yeah we're on a tight runway so main goal today is to understand per-token unit economics and what levers we have to hit our ops budget
[00:00:25] Priya: great. quick intro from our side too, i'm priya, i'll run through a bit of the batching/caching stuff and what we typically recommend for these workloads
[00:00:36] Sarah: just to set context, we do roughly 1.5M requests/day right now, avg prompt 120 tokens, avg generation 60 tokens, peak qps around 40. most calls are customer-facing chat and some reranking jobs
[00:00:50] Mark: infra constraints: we need VPC peering for private deployments, egress rules are locked down, and we have SOC2 requirements for logs retention

[00:01:10] Alex: cool. so at a high level, hosted gives the fastest time-to-value and per-token pricing with no infra overhead. dedicated is reserved GPU pools — predictability and lower unit cost at scale. private gives you VPC/on-prem control but higher fixed cost, right
[00:01:28] Tom: question on numbers — what's the delta in per-token between hosted and dedicated, ballpark?
[00:01:35] Priya: yeah so ballpark — hosted list price e.g. 0.0008 to 0.0012 per token for gen depending on model. with dedicated reserved capacity you typically see 20-40% lower unit cost because of reserved GPU amortization; if you add caching and quantization you can get another 20-50% effective savings on token spend
[00:01:55] Sarah: can you break down the caching bit — prefix KV cache, yes? how much real-world impact?
[00:02:05] Priya: absolutely. prefix caching for chat/assist workloads where prompts have repeated prefixes (system + few-shot) can drop token compute by 10-60% depending on repetition. KV cache for long-context reuse reduces autoregression work on subsequent calls — we see big wins on conversation with long histories. important note: cache hit rate is workload dependent, so we recommended providing a sample of prompt traces for benchmark
[00:02:32] Tom: ok, and batching — how much does our latency hit vs cost saving? our SLO is 150ms p95 for interactive chat
[00:02:40] Priya: continuous batching is workload-aware; for low latency SLOs we do micro-batching with small windows (5-15ms) — you get some throughput improvements without breaking 150ms p95 generally. bigger batching windows (50-200ms) help throughput but will increase p95; dedicated pools give more deterministic batching behavior so better unit economics while keeping p95 low

[00:03:10] Mark: on private, we have to run in our VPC and use our KMS, can redwood support HSM/KMS integration? also what's the audit log exposure?
[00:03:19] Alex: yes, private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations for key management, and audit logs can be routed to your SIEM. we'll send the SOC2 and VPC runbook docs — priya will attach the security pack
[00:03:33] Sarah: model variants — if we quantize we see reduced quality sometimes; what's your recommendation for trading quantization vs SLOs?
[00:03:41] Priya: we have quantization profiles per-model: int8 and mixed precision options. for retrieval-augmented generation we often use int8 + distillation to maintain quality. for customer-facing chat we recommend running a small eval set; accuracy delta is usually small for many open models, but depends — we'll run evals in the benchmark

[00:04:15] Tom: can you talk about the pilot? timeline and what you need from us to get meaningful numbers?
[00:04:23] Alex: pilot typically 2-4 weeks: week 1 on-boarding + traffic replay setup, week 2 run benchmarks/quality evals, week 3 tuning (batching, cache config), week 4 handoff with TCO. we need anonymized prompt traces, target SLOs, and a list of model candidates
[00:04:40] Tom: we can provide two weeks of traces, okay. budget-wise we'd like to see a projection that shows hosted vs dedicated TCO over 12 months
[00:04:49] Alex: yep we'll include a 12-month TCO spreadsheet. important lever to call out: reserved committed capacity reduces per-token but adds committed spend — we'll show break-even points for base QPS vs burst patterns

[00:05:10] [00:05:10] Speaker 2 (Priya): one real world example — a finance customer with ~3M req/day moved to dedicated and with batching + prefix cache lowered effective token spend by ~45% and p95 stayed within SLO because of deterministic pools. your numbers line up with opportunity
[00:05:30] Sarah: do you support model pinning/rollouts? we want A/B on model size for quality checks
[00:05:36] Alex: yes rollouts are standard — canary, A/B and automatic fallback policies. that also helps limit cost as you only route a small percentage to larger models initially

[00:05:52] Tom: what's the difference in support & SLAs between hosted and dedicated?
[00:05:58] Alex: hosted has standard support tiers; dedicated includes SLA-backed latency and uptime targets with a direct SE touch during onboarding. private includes enterprise support + on-prem packaging options

[00:06:12] Mark: any hidden costs we should watch for? egress? log retention?
[00:06:18] Priya: good callouts — egress and long retention of debug-level logs can add up. also large KV caches in-memory for very long contexts can affect instance sizing on private. we'll surface all of these in the TCO

[00:06:32] Sarah: can you quantify the batching/caching delta for our profile (1.5M req/day, 120/60 tokens)?
[00:06:40] Priya: rough calc offline now — with moderate cache hits (30%) and micro-batching we estimate 25-35% effective token cost reduction on hosted; with dedicated plus tuning you could reach 40-55% effective reduction. again subject to benchmark data

[00:07:05] [00:07:05] Alex: a practical approach — start hosted pilot to validate quality quickly, then for production evaluate dedicated if steady-state throughput justifies reserved capacity. private only if you need VPC/on-prem for compliance
[00:07:20] Tom: timeline — if we start pilot next week, what's realistic for a production readiness decision?
[00:07:27] Priya: 6-8 weeks from pilot start for a full production decision: 2 weeks pilot, 2 weeks tuning and load testing, then procurement for dedicated/private if chosen. that fits typical procurement cycles

[00:07:45] Mark: procurement note — procurement asks for unit rates and examples of committed tier pricing, can you share that?
[00:07:52] Alex: yes pricing deck will include committed tier discounts and example ROIs. we'll also show the cost model break-even graphs

[00:08:04] Sarah: any risks you often see during piloting?
[00:08:09] Priya: top ones: low cache hit rates due to prompt variance, token inflation from system messages, and misconfigured batching windows causing latency spikes. we test for these in the benchmark and add mitigations

[00:08:30] Tom: ok great. one more — for private deployment latency to our on-prem data stores, do you support local inference nodes vs centralized control plane?
[00:08:40] Alex: yes private supports local inference nodes with a customer-managed control plane; the control plane can be in your VPC or as a managed private control plane — we'll detail network topologies in the runbook

[00:08:55] [00:08:55] Speaker 1 (Tom): small transcription glitch — sorry for the background noise earlier

[00:09:05] Alex: no worries. let's do a quick recap and action list
[00:09:10] Alex: recap — we talked hosted vs dedicated vs private, batching and prefix/KV caching levers, quantization tradeoffs, pilot plan + TCO. next steps: we'll send pricing deck, TCO template, security docs; priya to schedule bench; tom to share traces
[00:09:28] Tom: yep that works
[00:09:31] Sarah: thanks everyone, we'll review the pricing and get traces over by end of week
[00:09:37] Mark: i'll confirm VPC constraints and send firewall rules
[00:09:40] Alex: perfect. thanks all, speak soon

[00:09:45] End of recording

Notes on transcription: minor mis-attributions in a few turns, some product names transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'dedicated pool' etc.
